Don't worry my dear, all blood is tested and anything that doesn't measure up is thrown out. For example, my father can't donate due to taking epilepsy medications twice daily for the past 40 years. The medication in his blood is unsafe for other people, despite him being in otherwise perfect health. Even if he lied on the questionnaire, and said he was on no medications, his blood would go through the same testing process all donated blood is put through and would be thrown away so as not to harm anyone receiving a transfusion. Blood with other impurities or risks such as blood from someone with HIV who was unaware of their condition during the time of donation is also removed.

People can't always know at all times if their blood is acceptable which is why it is tested. I have had to re-schedule donation twice due to anemia because the appointments were scheduled right after my menstrual cycle which tends to draw a lot more iron from me than usual (my doc speculates its due to the damage cause in my GI tract from a really horrible bout of food poisoning that caused a month of colitis... make sure you guys only eat properly cooked chicken ok? Shit fucks you up!) Other people can be bitten by a mosquito with malaria and have no idea by the time they go to donate.

Human error like this is normal so it is accounted for in the blood testing process. You will only receive safe, healthy blood in any transfusion.

edit: The reason why you have to describe any meds or conditions on questionnaires at all is simply to save time. They test ALL BLOOD so if they can turn away anyone whose blood is unfit before the donation process it saves a lot of time and money on the testing system. They also include a secret sticker on the final stage of the questionnaire where the nurse leaves you alone with two stickers, one that says in a secret, scannable code: "yes, use my blood" and one that says "my blood is unsafe" to put on the questionnaire. This is the last stage for someone to think "You know what, I have a hangover right now which means there must still be alcohol in my blood. Maybe this isn't a good idea after all, but I don't want anyone to know because I will be embarrassed/in trouble." That paper with that sticker will stay with your bag of blood until it gets to a centre where all blood marked by the donor as "unsafe" is removed and only the blood with the "safe" sticker ca proceed to testing.
